title: What Makes a Strong Model? A Unified Spectral Analysis of Knowledge Transfer over High-dimensional Linear Regression
claim: Transfer succeeds through two spectral mechanisms: a slower-decaying teacher expands the learnable spectrum, and a low-dimensional task lets the student filter noise.
layout: 4 panels in a row, left-to-right, rounded boxes with red annotations
description: Four rounded-box panels in a row, each a schematic plot, captioned (a) Assumption 2,3, (b) Theorem 3, (c) Assumption 5 and (d) Theorem 5. Panel (a) shows eigenvalue decay curves for the student (blue) and teacher (orange) over eigen dimension, with black arrows up to a dashed red target signal w*. Panel (b) shows bar charts of student (blue) and teacher (red) signal per eigen dimension. A large red 'Spectral Barrier' label and an orange arrow mark the point where the student's bars cut off. Panel (c) stacks two bar plots, a teacher (orange) and a student (green), each with a dashed red cutoff line k†. Panel (d) plots risk against n, with a brown R_T2S curve and a cyan R_Trans curve, plus a red 'Optimal Early Stopping' label and an orange arrow to the minimum. The red labels and orange arrows draw the eye first.
caption: In the KD regime, a teacher with slower spectral decay acts as a pre-conditioner to trigger Spectral Horizon Expansion, enabling the capture of statistically inaccessible high-frequency signals. In the W2S regime, a low task-specific intrinsic dimensionality allows the student to leverage its excess capacity for Spectral Denoising, filtering out optimization noise to recover the underlying geometry.
abstract: Teacher-Student Knowledge Transfer (KT) is ubiquitous in modern machine learning, ranging from classical model compression via Knowledge Distillation (KD) to the emergent phenomenon of Weak-to-Strong (W2S) generalization. While existing studies offer isolated insights, a unified theoretical framework explaining the efficacy of KT across these disparate regimes remains lacking. In this work, we establish a unified spectral analysis of SGD dynamics in high-dimensional linear regression, elucidating the efficiency of KT across seemingly disparate regimes. We characterize KT efficiency through two distinct mechanisms: \emph{Spectral Horizon Expansion} in KD, which enables the capture of statistically inaccessible high-frequency signals, and \emph{Spectral Denoising} in W2S, where the student acts as a filter for optimization noise. Our framework unifies these phenomena, revealing that the efficacy of transfer is governed by the interplay between implicit regularization and heterogeneous spectral learning speeds over the spectrum.
